hero.title: AFROEURO Soccer Academy
hero.subtitle: The public face of Afro Euro Sports Agency — a registered Tanzanian sports institution developing youth football with integrity.

legal.title: Legal registration
legal.body: Afro Euro Sports Agency is registered with the National Sports Council (Baraza la Michezo la Taifa, BMT) under registration number NSC 146.

story.title: Who we are
story.p1: Afro Euro Sports Agency exists to discover, nurture, and advance athletic talent in Tanzania toward international standards — while using sport to strengthen communities facing social and environmental challenges.
story.p2: Operating publicly as AFROEURO Soccer Academy, we combine structured youth development with education on health, discipline, and opportunity — helping young people lift themselves through football.

mission.title: Mission
mission.body: Empower talented youth to pursue scholarships and sustainable careers in sport through professional coaching, safeguarding, and transparent pathways.

vision.title: Vision
vision.body: A Tanzania where every committed young athlete — regardless of background — can access world-class training, honest mentorship, and real routes to education and employment.

impact.title: Social impact
impact.body: We use football to address poverty, health risks, and social pressures — including substance misuse — by teaching discipline, teamwork, and life skills alongside technical training.

partnerships.title: International relationships
partnerships.body: We have built relationships with clubs such as Azam FC, Valencia FC, and FC Barcelona’s academy network in Nigeria. We also engage with clubs across Norway, Sweden, Poland, and Hungary. Our players participate in international youth festivals and tournaments — including events in South Africa and Dubai — broadening perspective and ambition.

why.title: Why AFROEURO matters
why.body: Parents receive clarity on fees and schedules. Players train in a culture that demands excellence while protecting childhood. Partners meet an organization registered in Tanzania and committed to ethical development.

hero.title: Youth development program
hero.subtitle: Annual structure, weekly rhythm, holiday intensives, and clear expectations for every family.

mediaStrip.title: Training that looks and feels elite
mediaStrip.subtitle: Real sessions, real pitches, real development — the environment we build for every player.

overview.title: Program overview
overview.body: AFROEURO’s youth development program runs in two major phases each year: January through May, and July through November. Training is delivered three days per week to balance school, worship, and recovery while maintaining technical progress.

phases.title: Annual training calendar
phases.body:
Phase A: January – May.
Phase B: July – November.
Between phases we communicate clearly on breaks and optional activities so families can plan ahead.

weekly.title: Weekly schedule
weekly.body:
Training days: Wednesday, Saturday, and Sunday.
Saturday & Sunday mornings: 07:00 – 09:00 (local time).
Some groups may train in the evening on weekends to align with church commitments — your coach will confirm.
Wednesday sessions take place in the evening only.

holiday.title: Holiday training
holiday.body:
During school holidays, training runs Monday – Friday from 07:00 – 09:00. Weekends are rest days.
Two holiday windows are published each December (for example 1–15 December and 8–19 December) to reflect different school closing dates — confirm exact dates with the office each year.

requirements.title: What players need
requirements.body: Football boots (cleats), official academy uniform with our emblem, drinking water at every session, long football socks, and shin guards. Coaches may advise additional items as players progress.

safety.title: Child safety & guardians
safety.body: Every child must arrive and leave with an authorized guardian listed on the registration form. Pickup may only be performed by designated adults. A dedicated supervisor supports safeguarding during sessions.

health.title: Health & first aid
health.body: Medical information on the registration form must be accurate. Please disclose conditions such as heart disease, asthma, or sickle cell — never hide information that could affect your child’s safety. Qualified first aid support is available at training venues.

hero.title: Fees & payments
hero.subtitle: All figures in Tanzanian Shillings (TZS). Afro Euro Sports Agency publishes costs openly so families can plan with confidence.

fees.intro: Below are the official registration-related fees. The academy may communicate payment milestones — for example beginning with registration and first-aid contributions during an announced intake window.

initial.title: Current intake payment
initial.body: For the published intake period, families begin with the registration form and first-aid bundle below. Other items are scheduled as communicated by the office.
initial.deadline: Published through {date} — confirm with the academy if extended.

monthly.title: School-term training fee
monthly.body: When schools reopen, monthly training is billed at the rate below unless otherwise announced.

holiday.title: Holiday training program
holiday.body: Holiday intensives are billed per published window (typically two December phases). Fee shown is for the structured holiday program communicated each season.

once.title: Registration fees are not duplicated
once.body: Once the full registration package has been paid according to academy policy, those registration charges are not billed again for the same player.

cta.title: Questions?
cta.subtitle: Our office can walk you through payment timing, uniform fitting, and holiday options.

hero.title: Payment & support
hero.subtitle: Official CRDB payments for Afro Euro Sports Agency — plus ways partners strengthen youth development.

impact.title: What your payments enable
impact.body: Fees fund coaching, safeguarding, facilities, and tournament participation. Partners who wish to sponsor bursaries or equipment strengthen access for families who need extra support.

scholarships.title: Access & scholarships
scholarships.body: Directed support can help talented players cover fees or travel for international exposure.

equipment.title: Kit & facilities
equipment.body: Contributions maintain training quality — from balls and goals to safe playing surfaces.

travel.title: Tournaments abroad
travel.body: International festivals require careful planning; partners help make participation possible without compromising child safety.

bank.title: Official bank details
bank.subtitle: Use your child’s name or invoice reference in the transfer narration when instructed by the office.

instructions.title: After you pay
instructions.body: Email or WhatsApp your bank slip to the academy office so we can confirm receipt and update your player file. Reach out anytime if you need help with references.

thanks.title: Thank you
thanks.body: AFROEURO exists because families trust us with their children and because partners believe in Tanzanian talent. We steward every contribution with transparency.
